newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends below 2.0 percent, securities up.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends below 2.0 percent, securities up.

text.p: Indian call money rates ended lower at 0.75-1.25 percent on Wednesday, against the day's opening levels of 1.25-1.75 percent, dealers said.
Most deals were in the region of 1.25-1.50 percent, they said.
The next fortnight will see call rates move up, as six-year government paper and the 364-day treasury bill auctions take 40 billion rupees out of the system, a dealer said.
"Rates won't cross 5.0 percent levels, as the next repo auctions will attract less bidders and the repurchase of previous repo will fuel and improve current liquidity conditions," he said.
The securities market witnessed huge buying interest on Wednesday, a dealer said.
The year 2000 and 2004 maturity papers were in the limelight, he added.
The 13.80 percent government stock 2002 rose by 55 paise to 108.0 rupees, against the previous close, a dealer said.

The 12.59 percent stock 2004 continued its rally with the price touching 102.90 rupees against the previous close of 102.55 rupees, and the 12.50 percent 2004 stock rose to 102.75 rupees, from 102.35 rupees, he said.
Commercial paper with 1-month maturity was quoted at 7.25/ 7.50 percent, 2-month at 8.00-8.25 percent, while the 3-month maturity was quoted at 9.00-9.25 percent, a dealer said.
The certificate of deposit maturing in April 1998 was quoted at the 10.25/10.45 percent level, she added.
